messages:
alex: heads-up — running into runtime errors trying to use the JS SDK in a Cloudflare Workers sample app. errors: `process is not defined`, `require is not a function`, and some of our exported types mention Node-only types. onboarding flow broke for a user. any quick wins?

marta: ugh. same boat. bundler (esbuild) produced CJS-style output in one of our samples so workers tried to execute it and blew up.

sam: CF Workers is strict ESM + web APIs only. Our SDK currently ships both cjs and esm, but the cjs entry gets pulled in by some bundlers / old tsconfigs. we need a workers-targeted ESM build.

kai: can we just add a tiny runtime shim? e.g. polyfill `process.env` and `globalThis.Buffer`? i know CF doesn't want Buffer but a small shim that maps `Buffer.from` -> Uint8Array should be fine for a few helpers.

lin: careful: crypto is different. Cloudflare has Web Crypto; Node's `crypto.randomBytes` is not available. shimming that by delegating to `crypto.getRandomValues` is ok but types need to reflect that.

marta: also TypeScript consumers hit issues: our types reference `NodeJS.ReadableStream` in some helpers. that leaks Node types into final .d.ts. users on workers that `skipLibCheck` will still see errors.

alex: proposal: produce a new dist flavor `esm-edge` that: 1) is pure ESM, 2) targets web globals (no process, no fs, no Buffer), 3) uses Web Crypto and native fetch, 4) ships its own small d.ts that avoids Node types. then update sample app to import the `esm-edge` entry via import maps or `exports` condition.

sam: +1. practically: update package.json exports like:
```json
{
  "exports": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
    "." : "./dist/cjs/index.cjs",
    "edge": "./dist/esm-edge/index.mjs"
  }
}
```
then docs show `import sdk from 'redwood-sdk/edge'` for workers.

kai: two followups: 1) add a tiny runtime-check in the ESM code that throws a clear error if Node-only API is used (helpful DX), 2) ship a `polyfills/edge-shim.js` that sample apps can include to map minimal APIs when running in older environments.

lin: regarding types: generate a separate `dist/esm-edge/index.d.ts` that uses only DOM types + our types. simplest path is a JSDoc-driven build or a separate tsconfig that sets `lib: ["es2021","dom"]` and `types: []`.

marta: i tried a POC: changed tsconfig to `target: ES2022, lib: ["es2022","dom"]` and output to `dist/esm-edge`. Tests pass locally in Miniflare. sample app: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw-workers-sample/tree/edge-poc (internal link).

alex: great. next steps: 1) open two GH issues (edge build + types cleanup), 2) patch quick sample and update onboarding docs to use `import sdk from 'redwood-sdk/edge'`, 3) add a devex blurb about common CF errors and how to fix bundler configs.

devex-bot: created issues #824 (edge ESM build) and #825 (d.ts edge flavor) and assigned to @marta + @sam.

sam: i'll own #824. planning to add a `rollup`/`esbuild` step for `esm-edge` that strips requires and ensures no conditional node imports.

lin: i'll take #825 — will add a separate tsconfig + CI check that ensures `dist/esm-edge/index.d.ts` doesn't reference `NodeJS` types.

alex: perfect. can someone add a tiny note in onboarding checklist about "prefer /edge entry for CF Workers and other web-only runtimes"? that'd save support tickets.

marta: adding to docs backlog now. i'll link the POC sample and include a snippet for common esbuild flags: `platform: 'browser', target: 'es2022', format: 'esm'`.

kai: thanks! one more: let's include a short troubleshooting snippet in the sample README showing how to detect imports that pulled Node helpers: `grep -R "require(" dist | head` and `node -p "Object.keys(globalThis)"` for dev debugging.

alex: awesome, thanks all. will follow up in the GH issues with a small PR to update the sample.
